creator: Shalini Other Lady WFPB
text: Shalini shared a picture of a 'thaali' including Sarson Ka Saag and Makki ki roti. She mentioned a specific addition to her saag: 'I did add about 1/2 a cup of cooked cannellini beans before blending.'

creator: Uma Venkataraman WFPB
text: Uma suggests freezing broccoli stems, then cooking and blending them with a high-speed blender like a Vitamix to achieve a delicious creaminess. Shalini also noted that she likes them steamed or raw in salads.

recipe_name: Oil-Free Olives Discussion & Sodium Reduction Tip
creator: Gurmeet Singh Manku, WFPB member, Alpesh WFPB, Ankit Dangi WFPB, WFPB member
text: Gurmeet inquired about where to buy oil-free olives. Group members confirmed that canned black olives are often packed in water and are oil-free, though they typically contain salt. Alpesh mentioned that some brands at Whole Foods/Sprouts sell olives soaked in vinegar and salt. Ankit Dangi WFPB added that Whole Foods Market, including their 365 branded olives, offers several oil-free options, which also tend to contain salt. A tip was shared to reduce sodium by rinsing canned olives with water or soaking them for some time.

recipe_name: Radicchio Wraps with Lima Beans, Arugula, and Drumstick Soup
creator: Ankit Dangi WFPB, WFPB member
text: Ankit described a dish consisting of sautéed lima beans and arugula rolled in radicchio leaves, with drumstick soup served as a dip. The creator of the dish confirmed this method and suggested adding relish, chutney, or other condiments over the rolled radicchio wraps for enhanced flavor.

recipe_name: Pav Bhaji with Beets and Ezekiel Bread
creator: Alpesh WFPB, WFPB member
text: Alpesh's wife makes Pav Bhaji by adding beets to the bhaji to give it a red color. For the 'pav,' Ezekiel bread is used. Alternatively, Ezekiel biscuits (a thicker, round version of the bread, split in two) can be used. A group member also suggested putting pieces of Ezekiel bread in daal for a great taste.

recipe_name: Utilizing Beet Greens and Daikon/Muli Greens
creator: Shalini Other Lady WFPB
text: Shalini highlights beet greens and daikon/muli greens as underrated and delicious. She incorporates them into veggie juices and curries, noting their benefits without the extra sugar. She routinely asks farmers for these greens, sometimes receiving them for free, as many people discard them.

recipe_name: Air-fried Sweet Potato with Basic Spices
creator: WFPB member
text: Sweet potato is prepared by air-frying and adding basic spices.

creator: Shalini Other Lady WFPB
text: Curd rice is made using soy yogurt.

creator: Group Member
text: Dandelion leaves can be consumed in salads, particularly young ones. The roots are also edible and can be used to make tea. Leaves can be dried for tea as well. To make dandelions more palatable in salads, a dressing can be created by blending coconut water with macadamia nuts. Dandelion greens can also be juiced with celery and beets, which is beneficial for liver health and cholesterol control. It is important to ensure that dandelions are grown without pesticides.

creator: Ankit Dangi WFPB
text: When making khichdi with dals, Ankit does not soak the barley overnight. However, when using beans and/or other grains, he does soak them overnight.

creator: Gurmeet
text: Gurmeet shared a method for making misal powder by following a recipe from indianhealthyrecipes.com (https://www.indianhealthyrecipes.com/misal-pav-recipe/) and specifically skipping the dry coconut to make it WFPB compliant and oil-free.
